title: scarcode: reproduction package for "Scrambling, not athermality, protects quantum information under generic measurement: chaotic states outperform quantum many-body scar codes"

creators.name: Wakaura, Hikaru

creators.affiliation: QIRI (Quantum Integrated Research Institute Inc.), Tokyo, Japan

description: Reproduction package for the paper Scrambling, not athermality, protects quantum information under generic measurement: chaotic states outperform quantum many-body scar codes (H. Wakaura and T. Tanimae). Contains the scarcode Python package (PXP and spin-1 Schecter–Iadecola models, monitored-trajectory reference-qubit coherent information, static Knill–Laflamme diagnostics, emergent-su(2) Casimir), the paper-reproduction drivers, a pytest benchmark suite, all figure data, and the LaTeX manuscript source. One command regenerates every figure. Main finding: under every measurement we test, a logical qubit encoded in the PXP scar subspace carries less coherent information than an energy-matched thermal encoding, so scrambling rather than athermality is what protects encoded information; an exactly solvable spin-1 model isolates the Casimir variance as the control parameter, and only zero-variance exact scars are protected. MIT-licensed. Source repository: https://github.com/deeptell-inc/chaosec
notes: Software reproduction package for the article of the same name, submitted to Quantum (quantum-journal.org). Regenerate results with `pip install -e .` then the drivers in scripts/.
